lines.text: Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water!
Jack fell down and broke his crown, slipping on the slick winter ice!
Why is smooth ice so much more slippery than hard wooden floors?
At the very surface of ice, water molecules cannot hold onto each other tightly!
They form an ultra-thin layer of loose, slushy liquid water molecules!
When your warm boot steps down, that microscopic water layer acts like ball bearings!
There's almost zero friction, which lets your feet glide—or tumble down the hill!
Now you know the slippery physics behind Jack and Jill!
Tread carefully and subscribe to BabyBeats Rhymo for daily facts!
